content:
## Quick Overview: Krka National Park Facts

Krka National Park covers 109 km² in North Dalmatia, near Šibenik. It is about 85 km from Split, roughly a one-hour drive, which makes it the easiest national park day trip on the Dalmatian coast. Its main attraction is Skradinski buk, the last and longest of seven tufa barriers on the Krka River and the longest tufa barrier in Europe.

The park has several separate sections. Skradinski buk, Visovac Island and Roški slap are the three core stops. They are not connected by one internal transport system, so the order of the day matters.

## Krka Itinerary for 1 Day (Best Route)

### 08:00 – Arrive at Lozovac Entrance

Lozovac has a large free car park and a seasonal shuttle bus down to Skradinski buk. Drivers should use this entrance. In summer the park opens at 08:00, and arriving at opening time is the single most effective way to avoid crowds on the narrow boardwalks.

Buy tickets online in July and August if possible, and check the current price list before travelling.

### 08:30 – Skradinski buk Boardwalk Loop (1.5–2 hours)

The wooden walkways cross small islands and channels between cascades. Allow 1.5 to 2 hours for the full loop with photo stops. The site has two restaurants and an ethno village with souvenir shops, which is also where the old water mills are displayed.

Swimming at Skradinski buk has been banned since 1 January 2021, so do not plan the day around a swim here. At Roški slap, swimming is allowed only in the marked zones.

### 10:30 – Boat to Visovac (2 hours) or Roški slap (4 hours)

Boats leave from the Skradinski buk landing. Choose one:

- **Visovac only:** €15 adult, 2 hours return, with a 30-minute stop on the island to see the Franciscan monastery, church and museum.
- **Visovac + Roški slap:** €20 adult, 4 hours return, with 30 minutes on Visovac and about 90 minutes at Roški slap. The boat passes through the narrow Među gredam canyon.

Boat tickets are separate from the entrance ticket. Visovac monastery has no entrance fee of its own, but the general park ticket is required.

### 13:00 – Lunch and Final Walk

Eat at one of the two restaurants at Skradinski buk, or bring a picnic. Use the remaining time for the upper boardwalk sections, then return to the car by shuttle.

## Krka Itinerary for 2 Days

Two days remove the time pressure and allow the quieter northern sites.

**Day 1:** Skradinski buk in the morning, Visovac boat at 10:30 or later, then an evening in Skradin. Skradin is a small harbour town about 5 km by water from the falls, with restaurants along the waterfront.

**Day 2:** Drive to the Roški slap entrance (Laškovica). Walk the cascades known as Ogrlice (the necklace), then climb the 517 wooden steps up to Oziđana Cave. Continue to the Krka Monastery area or the Burnum Roman ruins, both covered by land-site tickets.

The Roški slap area has its own cheaper ticket: €7 in winter, €12 in April, May and October, and €20 in June to September for adults. Check whether your general ticket from day one covers day two; it normally does not, so plan to buy the cheaper area ticket for the second day.

## Krka National Park Ticket Prices (2027 Price List)

Prices below come from the park's official 2027 price list. The park can change prices, so confirm them on the official website before travel.

| Category | Jan–Mar, Nov–Dec | Apr–May, Oct | Jun–Sep |
|---|---|---|---|
| Adult, all land sites | €7 | €20 | €40 (€30 after 15:00) |
| Child 7–18 / student | €4 | €12 | €15 (€11.25 after 15:00) |
| Adult, Roški slap area only | €7 | €12 | €20 |
| Under 7 | Free | Free | Free |

The standard ticket usually covers the Skradin–Skradinski buk boat and the Lozovac shuttle when they operate. Longer excursion boats cost extra.

## Opening Hours by Season

Hours at Skradinski buk, from the park's published schedule (confirm before travel):

- June to August: 08:00 to 20:00
- May and September: 08:00 to 19:00
- April and 1–15 October: 08:00 to 18:00
- March and 16–31 October: 09:00 to 17:00
- November to February: 09:00 to 16:00 (closed 25 and 26 December)

From November to March the boats and shuttle buses do not run, so the visit is on foot or by your own car.

## Which Entrance Should You Use?

### Lozovac
Best for drivers. Large free car park, shuttle to Skradinski buk, and the easiest route to continue to Visovac and Roški slap by road.

### Skradin
Best for the scenic first arrival. The park boat from Skradin to Skradinski buk is included in the ticket from April to October. Parking in town is paid and limited, and you are tied to the boat schedule. The walking alternative is a 3.4 km trail along the river.

### Roški slap / Laškovica
Best for the middle section of the river. Tickets for boat tours can be bought here. Use it when the goal is Roški slap, Ogrlice and Oziđana Cave rather than the main falls.

## Boat Trips and Prices

| Trip | Duration | Adult | Child |
|---|---|---|---|
| Skradinski buk – Visovac – return | 2 h | €15 | €10 |
| Skradinski buk – Visovac – Roški slap – return | 4 h | €20 | €15 |
| Roški slap – Visovac – return | 2 h | €15 | €10 |
| Stinice or Remetić – Visovac – return | ~35 min | €10 | €7 |
| Skradinski buk – Čikola canyon | 45 min | €10 | n/a |

The Stinice and Remetić departures are the cheapest way onto Visovac, and they use parking areas on each side of the island.

## Best Time to Visit

May, June and September give strong water flow, warm weather and smaller crowds than August. July and August are the busiest months, and the €40 ticket applies. From November to March the park costs €7 and is nearly empty, but boats are off and hours are short.

In summer, the after-15:00 ticket at €30 is a real saving of €10, and late-afternoon light on the cascades is good. The trade-off is that the 2-hour and 4-hour boats may not fit before closing, so it works only for the walking loop.

## How to Get to Krka

- **From Split:** about 85 km, around 1 hour by car. Buses run to Skradin and cost roughly €10 to €15 one way.
- **From Šibenik:** the closest large town and a practical base.
- **From Zadar:** also workable as a day trip by car.
- **Organised tours:** typically €60 to €120 per person depending on inclusions.

## Local Tips That Save Time and Money

1. **Arrive at 08:00 and go to the falls first.** Tour buses from Split and Zadar usually reach the main boardwalks mid-morning.
2. **Walk the loop clockwise from the shuttle drop and look for side channels.** Most visitors stay on the main walkways and miss the quieter edges.
3. **Skip the 4-hour boat if you have a car.** This is the one excursion that sounds better than it is for drivers. Roški slap has its own road entrance and a cheaper area ticket, so paying €20 and spending four hours on a boat to see it is poor value when you can drive there in less time.
4. **Bring water, a hat and sandals with grip.** Boardwalks get wet and shade is patchy.
5. **Keep dogs on a leash.** This is required throughout the park.
6. **Check Roški slap in the afternoon.** Photos look better when the waterfall is out of shade.

## Where to Stay

Šibenik offers the widest choice, including the old town near the cathedral, and is roughly 15 km from the Lozovac entrance. Skradin suits visitors who want the boat arrival and an early start. Split works only as a day-trip base; the round trip is about 170 km.

## Sample Budget (per adult, 1 day, summer, self-drive)

- Entrance ticket: €40 (or €30 after 15:00)
- Visovac boat: €15, or Roški slap boat: €20
- Lunch at the park: roughly €15 to €25
- Parking at Lozovac: free

Total: about €70 to €85 before fuel.

faq.question: How many days do you need in Krka National Park?
faq.answer: One day covers Skradinski buk and a Visovac boat trip. Add a second day if you want Roški slap, Oziđana Cave and the Krka Monastery without rushing. If only Skradinski buk matters, about one to two hours is enough.

faq.question: How much does Krka National Park cost in 2027?
faq.answer: Adult tickets cost €7 from November to March, €20 in April, May and October, and €40 from June to September (€30 after 15:00). Children 7–18 pay €4 to €15, and under-7s are free. These are the official 2027 prices.

faq.question: Can you swim in Krka National Park?
faq.answer: Not at Skradinski buk, where swimming has been banned since 1 January 2021. At Roški slap, swimming is allowed only in the marked bathing zones; everywhere else, stay on the boardwalks.

faq.question: Which Krka entrance is best: Lozovac or Skradin?
faq.answer: Lozovac is better for drivers because of its large free car park and shuttle to Skradinski buk. Skradin is better for a scenic arrival, as the included park boat takes you to the falls from April to October.

faq.question: Is the Krka boat to Visovac and Roški slap worth it?
faq.answer: The €15 two-hour Visovac boat is worth it for most visitors. The €20 four-hour trip that adds Roški slap suits those without a car, while drivers can reach Roški slap by road more cheaply.

faq.question: How do you get from Split to Krka National Park?
faq.answer: Krka is about 85 km from Split, around one hour by car. Buses to Skradin cost roughly €10 to €15 one way, and organised tours cost about €60 to €120.

faq.question: What is the best time of day to visit Krka?
faq.answer: Arrival at opening time, 08:00 in summer, gives the emptiest boardwalks. In June to September the after-15:00 ticket is €30 and works well for a short walking visit, but it leaves too little time for the long boat trips.
